findings.title: Covered attention becomes enduring closure
findings.claim: Repeated turning away from the divine reminder becomes an enduring closure of receptive sight and hearing, while the focus ayah's plain statement that their eyes are covered and they cannot hear remains intact.
findings.mechanism: The reminder carrier at 18:101:7:1 meets the cover at 18:101:5:1 and the capacity/hearing pair at 18:101:10:1 and 18:101:11:1. The 18:57 and 20:124 connections supply wider refusal-to-closure evidence, and 18:11 supplies the distinct temporary cave-ear contrast.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the verse joins a covered eye to failed hearing: reception is portrayed as a condition that has closed, not as a single missed sound.
findings.containment: The 18:11 comparison is functional: the packet supports a contrast between temporary protective sealing and enduring incapacity, not an identity of events, a claim about cave duration, or a surah-wide thesis. The legacy reader walk remains corroborating and qualified.

epistemic.reason: The trusted cross-run record anchors all four focus branches and the exact focus occurrences; the legacy-unbound walk corroborates the same bounded relation without supplying an independent anchor.

findings.title: False protection reckoning under the cover
findings.claim: The covered reminder and failed hearing can sustain the false reckoning that servants independently protect, so the error concerns the evaluation of dependence as well as the reception of a reminder.
findings.mechanism: The cognitive-cover carrier at 18:101:5:1 meets the reminder and hearing occurrences at 18:101:7:1 and 18:101:11:1; the supplied 18:102 context acts as the wider trigger that exposes the mistaken protection calculation.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see how sensory closure reaches judgment: a covered receiver can preserve a false account of who protects and where dependence lies.
findings.containment: This is a qualified retrospective contextual inference from the supplied 18:102 relation. It does not establish a causal order beyond that record, turn the context into the focus's only meaning, or generalize the calculation beyond the named relation.

epistemic.reason: The reader walk names the exact focus-to-18:102 relation but is legacy_unbound and supplies no independent target morphology; the focus carriers and context trigger are retained with that limitation visible.

findings.title: The cover sustains mistaken evaluation
findings.claim: The concrete cover over the eyes becomes a cognitive filter that lets mistaken evaluation persist across worship and work, linking the false-protection calculation at 18:102 with the self-approving work calculation at 18:104.
findings.mechanism: The cover carrier at 18:101:5:1 meets the eye and reminder occurrences at 18:101:3:1 and 18:101:7:1; the supplied 18:102 and 18:104 contexts independently trigger the two forms of mistaken evaluation named by the wide reader walk.
findings.reader_payoff: The sensory failure becomes newly legible as a filtering mechanism for self-assessment: the problem is not only what reaches the senses, but what the blocked reception allows a person to keep calling good or sufficient.
findings.containment: This is a qualified wide-context inference from legacy reader material. The physical-cover and cognitive-veil facets remain distinct but connected; the packet does not establish a single causal sequence between the two contextual errors or a complete global system.

epistemic.reason: The wide reader walk supplies the focus branch refs and names both exact context ayahs, but its reader identity is legacy_unbound and the context projections do not supply target morphology; the inference is therefore retained with explicit qualification.
